title: Comparison of Polarized Versus Other Types of Endurance Training Intensity Distribution on Athletes' Endurance Performance: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis
authors: Silva Oliveira P, Boppre G, Fonseca H
population: Adults and young adults in interventions of >=4 weeks comparing polarized with other TIDs; 17 studies
findings: Polarized superior for VO2peak: SMD 0.24 (95% CI 0.01-0.48), 11 studies, n=284, I2=0%, GRADE high certainty.
VO2peak superiority occurred only in shorter interventions (<12 weeks; SMD 0.40, 95% CI 0.08-0.71, n=163) and in highly trained athletes (SMD 0.46, 95% CI 0.10-0.82, n=125).
No difference for time trial (SMD -0.01, 95% CI -0.28 to 0.25, n=221), time to exhaustion (SMD 0.30, 95% CI -0.20 to 0.79, n=66) or speed/power at VT2/LT2 (SMD 0.04, 95% CI -0.21 to 0.29, n=253).
Searched to 20 October 2022; PROSPERO CRD42022365117; RCT risk of bias rated as some concerns.
limitations: Pooled across sports (mostly cycling, skiing, rowing, running) and heterogeneous comparator TIDs; VO2peak is a surrogate, not race performance; search ends October 2022.
implications: Do not force polarization for performance outcomes (time trial, thresholds): the pooled effect is null.
If VO2max is the specific aim and the athlete is highly trained, a short (<12 week) polarized block is justified; otherwise default to a pyramidal, low-intensity-dominant layout.
Treat TID as an individual and phase-dependent choice, not a single optimum.

verification.notes: Crossref: Sports Med, online 2024-05-08, print Aug 2024. Researcher's '<=8 weeks' was wrong; PubMed abstract says shorter interventions are <12 weeks. Corrected, and the <12 week SMD added.
